newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks race ahead, Bombay at 20-month high.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks race ahead, Bombay at 20-month high.

text.p: Indian blue chips showed a smart rise on Tuesday taking a cue from yesterday's three percent rally as follow-up buying drove prices higher, traders said.
"The market is awash with liquidity," K.R. Bharat, country head at Credit Suisse First Boston told Reuters. "There is so much money going into the system."
Earlier in the day, Bombay stocks were bruised in early profit-taking but managed to rally higher towards the close.
Bombay's top 30-share index jumped 44.77 points, or 1.05 percent, to end at 4,300.86, hitting a 20-month high and adding gains to Monday's impressive three percent rally.
"The market is facing some resistance near the 4,300 level. It has come back from here, testing these levels a few times," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Securities.
Market action continued to be focussed on cement, financial institutions and multinational stocks, but the gains paled in comparision to the previous day's gains, traders said.

A sizzling 38 percent rally in the first half of 1997, largely led by foreign fund buying on attractive valuations, has made Indian stock exchanges the best performing Asian market this year, analysts said.

V.V. Sivakumar, research head Peregrine Capital said India has been the top performing market in Asia. "The outlook is still positive. The markets are still to run their full course ... it's just that the pace may wary."

"A 10 percent rise from these levels looks feasible. There are hopes of an economic turnaround. Clearly, we have to look ahead," said Gul Tekchandani, chief investment officer at Sun Foreign & Colonial Asset Management.
Analysts said the bullish outlook was based on falling interest rates, triggered by cuts last week in major banks' prime lending rates to 13.5 percent--the lowest in over 2 years.
